title: claude plugin eval (Claude Code plugin eval suites)

versions.pinnedIn: .github/workflows/ci.yml (npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.307; evals are not run in CI)

rules.rule: Keep --no-publish on every run of this suite.
rules.why: On a claude.ai subscription the HTML report is otherwise published as an artifact. It holds each case's prompt, every grader's rubric and pattern, and what Claude produced, so the planted defects and answer keys leave the machine.

rules.rule: Pass --scaffold only for this repo's own suites. Keep scaffold.sh to copying a fixture and running git init/commit, with the git identity set inline through -c flags.
rules.why: A scaffold runs as you, outside the agent sandbox, with a minimal environment: your PATH, HOME set to the run's temporary home, TMPDIR and a few constants. Your global git config and shell variables are absent. A scaffold that needs them, that exits non-zero, or that runs past 120 s makes the run score 0 with 'scaffold failed'.

rules.rule: Never rely on project configuration that a fixture or profile places in the workspace: .claude/settings*, CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/*.md and .mcp.json do not load in a run. Ship anything a case depends on in the plugin under test. Files the plugin's own skills and hooks Read, such as .stackfoundry/*, are plain files and still work.
rules.why: Project-scoped configuration is not read anywhere in a run, even when a scaffold_script wrote it. A case that assumes a rulebook or setting loaded is grading behaviour Claude never saw.
where: fixtures/*.profile/.stackfoundry/ (plain files; no .claude/rules or settings in profiles yet)

rules.rule: Grant Bash, Write, Edit, WebFetch and WebSearch with --allow-tools on the command line, and narrow the grant with --case. Listing them in allowed_tools is not enough.
rules.why: allowed_tools grants only the read-only set (Read, Glob, Grep, Skill, Agent, ...). Any other tool without a grant is removed from the session and shows as 'not granted'. A --allow-tools grant applies to every case in the run, so a broad grant widens the read-only cases too.

rules.rule: Run cases that need Bash only on a host with a sandbox backend (Linux with bubblewrap and socat, macOS, or WSL2), and tag them needs-bash.
rules.why: With Bash granted on a host that has no sandbox backend, which includes native Windows, Claude Code refuses each run. The case shows a run error and usually scores 0, which looks like a plugin regression.

Those options take a list or an optional path, so a target written after them is read as their value: as an extra tag or tool, or as the --json output path, which fails with 'output path must end in .json'.

rules.rule: Grade what a file contains with target or focus { source: file, path: ... }. Use target: files and file_exists only to ask which paths Claude created.
rules.why: files and file_exists see only paths created during the run. They miss files the scaffold created and files Claude only modified, so a 'nothing else changed' check built on them passes when an existing file was overwritten.

rules.rule: Mark graders that only the plugin can satisfy arm: with-only, such as dispatching a plugin agent or the effect of a plugin hook. Set arm: both on a 'must not happen' check that should count in the baseline too.
rules.why: Unmarked, such a grader scores the without-arm toward zero and inflates delta. tool_used: Skill graders are excluded automatically. When every grader in a case is excluded, all of them are scored normally.

rules.rule: Give each case one grader on the result and one on the process (tool_used or tool_order). Use regex for long output, and keep llm graders for short output with concrete PASS and FAIL conditions.
rules.why: An llm judge votes 2 of 3 and drifts more the longer the text it reads. Without a process grader you cannot tell whether the plugin produced the answer.

rules.rule: Write grader and input_match patterns as JavaScript regex: put case-insensitivity in flags: i, never inline (?i). Against target: trace, match JSON-escaped text (\" for a quote).
rules.why: An inline (?i) is not supported, and the trace is one JSON message per line, so a pattern written for the raw text silently fails to match.

rules.rule: Use only the documented prompt.md keys (schema_version, name, description, tags, plugins, runs, expected_outcome, model, max_turns, timeout_seconds, allowed_tools, append_system_prompt, env, and disallowed_tools since 2.1.299). Give each case.yaml schema_version "1.1" and name, and give each case at least one grader. Set max_turns and timeout_seconds explicitly.
rules.why: An unknown key or a case without graders fails to load, and the command exits 1. The defaults (10 turns, 300 s) cut multi-agent skills short, and hitting a cap is recorded as a run error.

rules.rule: Treat --runs 1 as a smoke check and confirm at the default 3 runs before a release. Pin --model and --judge-model whenever scores are compared over time.
rules.why: One run of a non-deterministic agent says little. A model rollout between two runs otherwise looks like a plugin regression or an improvement.
where: plugins/stackfoundry/evals/README.md (--runs 1, default three before a release)

rules.why: A suite costs roughly cases x runs x 2 agent runs, plus three judge calls per llm grader per run, on your plan or API bill. The ceiling is a list-price estimate checked before each run starts. Runs already in flight finish, and the command exits 2 with partial results.

rules.rule: Run the suite with a path target from a clone (cd plugins/stackfoundry; claude plugin eval .), never by naming the installed plugin.
rules.why: A named target reads the cases from the installed copy, and its results go under the current directory. The scaffolds reach ../../../../fixtures/, which exists only in a clone, so every scaffolded run fails.

bugCategories.name: vacuous-pass-without-grant
bugCategories.lookFor: A 'must not' grader (tool_used with min: 0 and max: 0, regex not_contains on a file) in a case whose tool needs --allow-tools, run without that grant. For example: running claude plugin eval . without --allow-tools Edit Write makes guard-blocks-generated-edit/file-untouched pass because Edit was never available, not because the hook denied it. check-updates no-installs passes trivially when Bash is not granted.
bugCategories.failure: A safety check reports PASS for a guard that never ran, so a broken hook or a mutating skill ships.

bugCategories.name: modification-invisible-to-grader
bugCategories.lookFor: A 'nothing else changed' assertion built only from target: files, file_exists or tool_used Edit, while Write or Bash is granted. A Write overwrite or a Bash redirect into an existing package.json or lock file goes undetected. The report-only cases pair nothing-else-created with a file-content check (pins-unchanged), a Write grader outside the report folder and a shell-write grader.
bugCategories.failure: A report-only skill that rewrites manifests passes its data-integrity eval.

bugCategories.name: delta-inflated-by-plugin-only-grader
bugCategories.lookFor: A grader the baseline can never pass (dispatching stackfoundry:<agent>, a hook's denial message) without arm: with-only. Or a case whose graders are all excluded, so they are scored normally after all.
bugCategories.failure: The without-arm is scored near zero and delta overstates what the plugin contributes.

bugCategories.name: scaffold-environment-assumption
bugCategories.lookFor: A scaffold.sh or scaffold-lib.sh change that reads shell variables, the global git config, the network, or tools not on PATH, or that can run past 120 s. A relative path that breaks when the script runs from the installed copy.
bugCategories.failure: Every run of the case scores 0 with 'scaffold failed'. This is misread as a plugin regression.

bugCategories.name: fixture-config-not-loaded
bugCategories.lookFor: A fixture or *.profile that adds .claude/settings.json, .claude/rules/*.md, CLAUDE.md, .mcp.json or hooks, and a case that expects Claude to obey them.
bugCategories.failure: The case grades behaviour against instructions Claude never received. It fails, or it passes for the wrong reason.

bugCategories.name: answer-key-reachable
bugCategories.lookFor: A change to copy_tree that drops the EXPECTED.md exclusion, an answer key copied under another name, or an expected result written into prompt.md, the fixture or the profile. The docs hide only the eval directory from the agent, not fixtures/ at the repo root.
bugCategories.failure: The agent reads the expected finding, and the eval measures copying instead of the skill.

bugCategories.name: api-error-read-as-regression
bugCategories.lookFor: A low score or non-zero exit where run errors show a rate or usage limit. Since 2.1.299 such runs score 0 without grading, and the baseline runs count too.
bugCategories.failure: A plugin change is reverted for a quota problem.

testing.layers: The eval suite is itself the behavioural harness for skills, agents and hooks. Each case runs a fresh claude -p session with only the plugin loaded, with and without the plugin, and graders score the transcript and files. Plugin structure is proved separately by claude plugin validate --strict and the unittest suite. Evals do not replace those checks.
commands: cd plugins/stackfoundry && claude plugin eval . --scaffold --runs 1 --no-publish --tag read-only
cd plugins/stackfoundry && claude plugin eval . --scaffold --runs 1 --no-publish --case guard-blocks-generated-edit --allow-tools Edit Write
cd plugins/stackfoundry && claude plugin eval . --scaffold --runs 1 --no-publish --case surveyor-splits-app-models --allow-tools Bash Write   (sandboxed host only)
cd plugins/stackfoundry && claude plugin eval . --case <case> --runs 1 --ablation none --no-publish   (iterate on graders, half the cost, no delta)
add --keep-temp to inspect what a run produced
traps: Default --threshold is 1.0: the command exits 1 when any case is below perfect.
A grader shown passed: false under a 1.0 run is an excluded (scored: false) grader, not a failure.
'Agent type stackfoundry:<agent> not found' in baseline runs is expected.

The first run against a directory asks 'Trust this plugin directory?'. Inside a git repo, yes trusts the whole repo. Under --json or without a terminal the run is refused unless --trust-plugin is passed.
git older than 2.31 stops the suite before any case runs (checked since 2.1.283).
Results go to evals/results/<timestamp>/ (git-ignored by **/evals/results/ in .gitignore).

A new case needs: the folder name equal to name, case.yaml with schema_version "1.1" if it scaffolds, a needs-bash or read-only tag matching its tools, one result grader and one process grader, and a row in evals/README.md.

wiring.check: Each skill-fired input_match names a skill folder that exists under plugins/stackfoundry/skills/, in the form '"skill"\s*:\s*"(?:stackfoundry:)?<name>"'.
wiring.failure: The Skill indicator never fires, and the case reports the skill as not chosen.

wiring.check: Each Agent input_match names an agent that exists as plugins/stackfoundry/agents/<name>.md, namespaced stackfoundry:<name> (the plugin.json name).
wiring.failure: A dispatch grader that can never pass.

wiring.check: Each scaffold.sh resolves SCAFFOLD_LIB to <repo>/fixtures/scaffold-lib.sh (four levels up from the case directory), and the named fixture, plus <fixture>.profile for with-profile, exists under fixtures/.
wiring.failure: The scaffold exits non-zero and the run scores 0.

wiring.check: Cases are found by auto-detecting the nearest enclosing plugin (plugins/stackfoundry/.claude-plugin/plugin.json). If W/OUT is missing or 'no plugin resolved' appears, add plugins: ["../.."] to prompt.md.

performance.note: Use -j/--concurrency (1-8) to shorten wall-clock time. Runs share the account's rate limit, so throughput does not rise past it, and runs that hit the limit score 0.

security.note: Running claude plugin eval loads the plugin's hooks, skills and agents and runs scaffolds as you, outside the sandbox. Run isolation limits only the agent under test. The plugin's own hooks (hooks/hooks.json guard) run outside the sandbox and could modify the files graders read. A passing suite says nothing about whether the plugin is safe.

A bare WebFetch or WebSearch grant (check-updates-report-only) lets the agent reach the web directly. Network rules from the sandbox apply only to shell commands. Fetched pages can carry prompt injection into a run that also holds Write and Bash. Prefer WebFetch(domain:...) grants for the registries the case needs, and run Bash-granting cases only on a sandboxed host.
where: plugins/stackfoundry/evals/README.md check-updates-report-only (--allow-tools Bash Write WebFetch WebSearch)

security.note: Before each run, eval switches off git hooks, credential helpers and other programs that git configuration can start, through GIT_CONFIG_COUNT. This needs git 2.31 or later, and Claude Code enforces it since 2.1.283. It matters because every scaffold here creates a git repository. No advisory found mentions plugin eval. The sandbox-escape advisories that were found (for example a git worktree path confusion, fixed in 2.1.163) predate eval's minimum version 2.1.269, so the 2.1.307 pin is above them.

pins: @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.307 in .github/workflows/ci.yml (used for claude plugin validate; evals run locally with whatever claude is installed)
lockStep: git >= 2.31 on the machine running evals
sandbox backend (bubblewrap + socat on Linux, macOS, or WSL2) for Bash cases

notReached: CHANGELOG entries for 2.1.269-2.1.295 were not read. The file is over 1.1M characters and only versions 2.1.296-2.1.319 were read. The docs page records the 2.1.283 git check and the 2.1.299 API-error scoring.
Full GitHub security advisory pages for claude-code were not opened, apart from CVE-2026-55607. The other advisories are known only from search snippets and are not cited.

The plugin CLI reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/cli-reference) and the sandboxing page were not fetched. Their eval-relevant content is summarised on the plugin-evals page, which is the page cited.
questions: evals/README.md says a sign-in stored for the desktop app or shell does not reach eval runs and asks for a token in the environment. The docs say runs use 'the same authentication and model provider your normal Claude Code sessions use' and pass an allowlist of provider and auth variables through. Keep the README's token advice as-is, or reword it to match the docs?

check-updates-report-only cannot detect a Write or Bash overwrite of an existing file: nothing-else-created sees only created paths, and no-edits covers only Edit. Add a regex grader on the contents of package.json and the lock file (source: file, not_contains a changed version), or a tool_used Write grader with an input_match that excludes docs/dependency-reports/?

The README says to run needs-bash cases 'there or in CI', but CI does not run evals. Is a CI eval job with --trust-plugin, pinned --model and --judge-model, and --max-cost-usd wanted, or is the README wording to change?

guard-blocks-generated-edit passes file-untouched vacuously when run without --allow-tools Edit Write. Should it get a process grader, such as tool_used Edit with min: 1 and arm: with-only, to prove the hook actually denied an attempt?
